Improved turbine durability and performance and reduced development cost will result from improved methods of predicting turbine metal temperatures.

The experimental approach progresses from fundamental experiments to more realistic cold, warm, or hot cascades, warm turbine, large low-speed turbine, or transient turbine tests, and finally real-engine or real-engine type turbine tests.

The analytical approaches start with relatively simple mathematical models and progress to more realistic cases that include more interactive effects, and finally combine all the interactive effects of the turbine operating in the real engine environment.
Very little or none of the experimental research information exists with controlled warm or real-engine type conditions and known boundary conditions.
The Airfoil Metal Temperature Runoff effort will use NASA conceived profiles and no film cooling initially.
